summary: Backend-only independent verification of P0.1-B4 (settlement lifecycle, webhook inbox, reconciliation, outbox) + P0.1-B5 (asset registry, monetary precision, maker-checker, recovery) with TRUE concurrency (threads + threading.Barrier), crash-window simulation via direct DB manipulation, and FULL serial regression of B1/B2/B3. New suite /app/backend/tests/test_p01b45_settlement_makerchecker.py = 46 tests, 45 PASS / 1 FAIL (the failure is a genuine defect: provider webhooks are not scoped to the provider in the URL). Full repo regression run serially (-n 0): 179 tests, all green after updating 2 stale capability assertions (outbox_events PLANNED -> PARTIAL, an intentional B4 status change). VERIFIED single-effect / single-winner: 100 identical webhooks (same event_id) -> exactly 1 'processed' + 99 'duplicate_ignored', 1 inbox row, exactly 1 SETTLED history row; 15 concurrent distinct 'settled' webhooks x 3 rounds -> exactly 1 'applied:SETTLED' + 14 'ignored_terminal' every round; 20 concurrent checker approvals x 2 rounds -> exactly 1x200 + 19x409, execution_status EXECUTED and exactly 1 Financial.MakerCheckerExecuted event; 12 concurrent reconciliation resolves -> 1x200 + 11x409; 12 concurrent rejects -> 1 winner. VERIFIED settlement is a pure tracking layer (ledger_entries count unchanged across create+submit), double submit -> 409 INVALID_TRANSITION_FROM, duplicate settlement for same tx returns the SAME settlement_id (unique idempotency_key), history = [PENDING, SUBMITTED]. Out-of-order: 'processing' after 'settled' -> ignored_terminal, terminal never overwritten; 'processing' on PROCESSING (non-applicable, non-terminal) -> REQUIRES_REVIEW; 'settled' directly on PENDING allowed. Reconciliation opens missing_provider_reference / amount_mismatch(HIGH) cases, is re-run idempotent (no duplicate OPEN case), invalid resolution -> 400, unknown case -> 409. Outbox: all settlement events reach DELIVERED via the background worker, unique indexes present on outbox_events.event_id / outbox_consumed.event_id / webhook_inbox(provider,provider_event_id), 5x replay keeps outbox_consumed count at exactly 1, replay of unknown event -> 404, injected DEAD_LETTER event is flagged CRITICAL by recovery scan and pushes financial-health severity to HIGH. B5: /api/assets returns JCC+EUR (decimals 2, minor_unit 100, HALF_UP), precision dry-run reports ledger_postings_checked/balances_checked and representable=true on clean data, repeated fractional debits (0.1 / 0.2 / 0.05) leave the balance minor-exact (99.65). Maker-checker: non-sensitive op -> 400 OPERATION_NOT_SENSITIVE, non-admin -> 403, maker approving/rejecting own request -> 403 MAKER_CANNOT_BE_CHECKER (backend-enforced), different admin -> executes (fee_policy actually written to settings and read back via GET /api/admin/fees), expired approval -> 409 APPROVAL_EXPIRED (and counted by recovery scan), tampered payload -> 409 PAYLOAD_TAMPERED with no side effect, unknown approval -> 404. manual_ledger_adjustment goes through the ledger: single 2-leg entry (acct_cash_x +25 / acct_sys_clearing -25) summing to 0, user balance 100 -> 125, ledger_balanced + jcc_supply_reconciled still true. Recovery crash windows: stale PROCESSING idempotency (20 min old) blocks a retry with 409, scan flags it AUTO_RECOVERABLE, auto-heal clears it, the retry with the same Idempotency-Key then succeeds and a second retry replays the cached response (no double debit, balance 90); an overdue ACTIVE hold is excluded from available balance by lazy expiry BEFORE any heal, and when nobody reads the wallet the scan reports expired_active_holds=1 and auto-heal marks it EXPIRED with held_cc back to 0 and NO double-decrement on a second heal (holds integrity healthy); a settlement backdated 30h is reported stuck (MANUAL_REVIEW) and in financial-health.settlements.stuck. Final invariants: ledger_balanced true, per_asset_sum JCC=0.0, jcc_supply_reconciled true, holds_health.healthy true, requires_review 0, outbox.dead_letter 0, severity INFO. Capability honesty confirmed exactly as specified (asset_registry/maker_checker/recovery_engine/reconciliation REAL; settlement_engine/outbox_events/monetary_precision PARTIAL; provider_adapters/card_issuing MOCK; stripe SANDBOX; invest/crypto/fx PLANNED).

critical.issue: Provider is NOT verified against the settlement: the handler does db.settlements.find_one({'provider_reference': ref}) without scoping to the {provider} path param. Reproduced: a settlement created with provider='mock_bank' was driven to SETTLED (terminal, irreversible) by a webhook posted to /api/webhooks/mock_processor -> result 'applied:SETTLED'. Since the webhook endpoint is PUBLIC and has NO signature/HMAC verification at all, anyone who learns or guesses a provider_reference can force any settlement into a terminal state. FIX: find_one({'provider': provider, 'provider_reference': ref}) plus a per-provider shared-secret/signature check before processing. Failing regression test: tests/test_p01b45_settlement_makerchecker.py::TestSettlementLifecycle::test_cross_provider_webhook_scope

minor.issue: No signature/HMAC/timestamp verification on the public webhook endpoint (acceptable while provider_adapters=MOCK, but must be added before any real provider). Also the inbox stores payload_hash but never compares it: a replay of the same event_id with a DIFFERENT body is silently 'duplicate_ignored' instead of being flagged as a payload conflict.

Not crash-safe between the SUBMITTED transition and the provider_reference write: if provider.submit() or the follow-up update fails, the settlement stays SUBMITTED with provider_reference=null forever (submit can no longer be retried -> 409). It is detected by reconciliation as missing_provider_reference (verified), but there is no retry/compensation path.

Dead code: the `for k in ('stale_idempotency','expired_approvals'): pass` loop with a 'log to journal' comment does nothing. expired_approvals and unprocessed_inbox are counted but never classified into AUTO_RECOVERABLE/MANUAL_REVIEW/CRITICAL, so an expired approval or an unprocessed inbox row produces a finding with an empty classification.

dry_run=false behaves identically to dry_run=true (no migration is implemented) — consistent with monetary_precision=PARTIAL, but the parameter is misleading; consider rejecting dry_run=false with 501 until implemented.

Now atomic (iteration_6 defect FIXED and re-verified green), but there is still no compensation if add_transaction / ledger_post fails AFTER the pending->rejected flip: the user would be left rejected without a refund and nothing flags it.
outbox_events / outbox_consumed grow unbounded (966 DELIVERED rows already in the preview DB) — no TTL index or archival.

action_items: CRITICAL: scope the webhook settlement lookup to the URL provider (find_one({'provider': provider, 'provider_reference': ref})) and add per-provider signature verification on POST /api/webhooks/{provider}. Keep test_cross_provider_webhook_scope as the regression test.
Compare the stored webhook payload_hash on duplicate event_id and open a reconciliation/review case on mismatch instead of returning duplicate_ignored.
Add a retry/compensation path for submit_settlement when the provider call or the provider_reference write fails (currently permanently SUBMITTED with no reference).
Classify expired_approvals and unprocessed_inbox findings in recovery_scan (and remove the dead `pass` loop).
Add compensation to admin reject if the refund postings fail after the atomic status flip.
Add a TTL/archival policy for outbox_events and outbox_consumed.
Split server.py (2331 lines) into routers — still outstanding from iterations 5/6 and now 3x over the 700-line guideline.
critical_code_review_comments: provider_webhook trusts the body's provider_reference without binding it to the {provider} path segment; combined with an unauthenticated public endpoint this is the only exploitable path found to force a terminal settlement state.

settlement_transition is a textbook single-document conditional find_one_and_update keyed on the allowed predecessor set — verified single-winner under 15-way concurrency and immune to terminal overwrite; the same pattern in approve_approval (status PENDING + maker_id $ne checker) is verified single-execution under 20-way concurrency.

Settlement correctly never posts ledger value (asserted by comparing ledger_entries counts) and _execute_approved_operation routes manual_ledger_adjustment through ledger_post with a balanced 2-leg entry — invariants stayed green.
financial_health severity model is sound (CRITICAL on ledger/supply/holds, HIGH on requires_review/high-severity cases/dead-letter) and was observed flipping to HIGH on an injected DEAD_LETTER event.
recovery_auto_heal is idempotent (verified: second run does not double-decrement held_cc) because _terminate_hold is itself a conditional update.

success_rate.backend: 224/225 (B4/B5 suite 45/46; full serial regression 179/179 after stale capability assertions were updated) — the single failure is the cross-provider webhook defect

All deleted in fixture teardown; settlements / webhook_inbox rows / reconciliation cases / approval requests created by the suite are also deleted. Post-run verification: 0 TEST users/sessions/txs/withdrawals/holds/refunds/reversals/ledger entries, 0 settlements, 0 open reconciliation cases, 0 pending approvals, 0 PROCESSING idempotency records, fee_policy reset to {}.
test_credentials: Emergent Google auth; tests seed user+session in Mongo (Authorization: Bearer <session_token>) per /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Maker-checker needs TWO distinct is_admin users (conftest._mk_user with is_admin=True twice).
context_for_next_testing_agent: New suite: /app/backend/tests/test_p01b45_settlement_makerchecker.py (46 tests, run SERIALLY with -n 0; it mutates global settings.fee_policy, settlements, outbox and admin integrity endpoints). Only failing test = TestSettlementLifecycle::test_cross_provider_webhook_scope (cross-provider webhook spoofing) — do NOT weaken it; it should pass once the provider is included in the settlement lookup. Helper fire(fn, n) uses threading.Barrier for true simultaneity. The 'tracker' fixture cleans settlements/cases/approvals/webhooks; deleting settlements can orphan reconciliation_cases (I removed 3 orphans manually) — prefer cancelling settlements over deleting when a case exists. Note: any GET /api/wallet by the hold owner lazily expires overdue holds, so to exercise the auto-heal branch you must NOT read the wallet first (see test_auto_heal_expires_hold_without_lazy_read). Stale capability assertions in test_p01b2_holds.py and test_p01b3_fees_refunds_reversals.py were updated to outbox_events=PARTIAL. Full regression: `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -n 0` ~ 280s, 179 green.
rca_of_the_issue: provider_webhook(provider, request) resolves the target settlement with db.settlements.find_one({'provider_reference': ref}) — the {provider} path segment is stored in webhook_inbox but never used as a filter, and there is no signature verification because the endpoint must stay public. Consequence: any caller (or a compromised/second provider) that knows a provider_reference can post {'event_id': <new>, 'provider_reference': <ref>, 'status': 'settled'} to /api/webhooks/<any-registered-provider> and the settlement transitions to SETTLED, which is terminal and therefore irreversible through the state machine (all further webhooks return ignored_terminal). Reproduced deterministically: mock_bank settlement + webhook to /api/webhooks/mock_processor -> result 'applied:SETTLED'. Mitigation: (1) add 'provider': provider to the find_one filter so a mismatch falls through to no_action (or better, opens a reconciliation case), and (2) verify a per-provider HMAC signature header before inserting into webhook_inbox.
